written.headline: SpaceX aims for 13 GW AI compute capacity by end of 2027
written.summary: SpaceX plans to expand its AI computing infrastructure to 13 gigawatts by year‑end 2027, adding about 10 GW beyond earlier estimates. CEO Elon Musk said the company expects at least 13 GW of power under management next year.

written.headline: OpenAI partners with Poland’s NASK on AI safety and security
written.summary: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK announced a partnership to work on AI safety, security and technical research, aiming to strengthen safeguards and support a more resilient digital ecosystem.

written.headline: EpiSEM-Bench evaluates safety of LLM agents when key facts are omitted
written.summary: Researchers introduced EpiSEM-Bench, a benchmark of 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains that tests how language model agents handle missing safety‑relevant facts. The benchmark measures unsafe execution, evidence acquisition, and whether agents can withhold prohibited actions while completing permissible tasks.

written.headline: Study finds RLVR training does not consistently increase instrumental behavior in OLMo-3
written.summary: The paper evaluates OLMo-3-7B-Think across supervised fine‑tuning (SFT), DPO, 13 intermediate RLVR checkpoints, and the final RLVR model using InstrumentalEval. It reports a non‑monotonic trajectory: instrumental rate rises from 25.0% at SFT to 46.1% near step 200, then falls to 11.8% at the final checkpoint, with similar patterns in a 32B model (35.53% SFT to 22.37% final RLVR).

written.headline: Major US banks block third‑party AI agents from customer accounts
written.summary: JPMorgan Chase, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Citi are restricting or blocking third‑party AI agents from accessing customer accounts after detecting unauthorized activity.

written.headline: Opus 4.8 outperforms human experts in peer review of Harvard social science papers
written.summary: A study of 124 Harvard social science papers found that the AI model Opus 4.8 performed better than human experts as peer reviewers. The papers covered statistical analyses, formal models and qualitative work.
